newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 17.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Feb. 17:

WASHINGTON - Julius Becton Jr., the retired Army general hired by the D.C. financial control board to replace the city's former superintendent of schools, says the school system's workforce has been shaped and dominated by cronyism.

WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration has been working to improve U.S. relations with North Korea, offering privately to ease some trade sanctions, to help organize donations of humanitarian aid, and to open the first U.S. diplomatic office in the North Korean capital, U.S. officials say.
WASHINGTON - Many Republicans remain uneasy about House Speaker Newt Gingrich and say he may have trouble staying in power if his standing has not improved noticeably before summer.
WASHINGTON - Last year's fatal crash of a Maryland commuter train and an Amtrak train has prompted a variety of new rules and standards to prevent future collisions.

WASHINGTON - A 1994 federal auction of hundreds of licenses to offer interactive television has proven to be a bad dream for women and minority business owners, as well as the Federal Communications Commission.
NEW YORK - The American Jewish community faces a serious rift of historic proportions over the "Who is a Jew" debate raging in Israel.
